Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Any man who leads a people in prayer, upon him is that he sits after the Taslim (greeting), and he does not leave that place until those behind him, who were preceded (in prayer), complete their prayer. That is obligatory upon every Imam when he knows that among them is one who was preceded, and if he knows that there is no one among them who was preceded in prayer, then let him go wherever he wishes.'

key_terms.مَسْبُوق: One who joined the prayer late and missed part of it

ai.seo_question: What should an Imam do after the congregational prayer if some followers joined late?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Imam’s duty of care (i'tibar) towards the congregation, ensuring the latecomers (Masbuqun) can complete their prayers without distraction or confusion. It highlights the scholarly principle that the Imam’s presence post-salam serves a functional role in maintaining congregational order, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the leader's attentiveness to the community's varying states. This ruling is particularly significant in contexts where the distinction between individual and congregational prayer completion is critical for legal validity.
